lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Today, we build a cluster that looks like your site.
A fresh sind cluster runs everything as root, with no Slurm accounts and no job limits. Your site has both, so a job that passes here can still fail there.
Say you're an admin or a research software engineer, and you want a cluster shaped like your site to test against.
We'll write one config file in four steps: the nodes, their limits, users with Slurm accounts, and software from CVMFS. Then we create the cluster.
All you need is sind and Docker, plus CVMFS on the Docker host for the last step.
Every config starts with kind Cluster. The nodes line lists the roles: a controller, a db node for accounting, a submitter as the login node, and three workers.
The defaults section sets limits for every node, here two CPUs each. Memory works the same way, and is five hundred twelve megabytes unless you set it.
On a managed worker, Slurm sees the same numbers, as the CPUs and memory of the node.
First, a word on Slurm accounting. slurmctld reports every job to slurmdbd, on the db node, which keeps the records in a database.
An association ties a user to an account, on a cluster. It can carry limits, like a cap on jobs, or on CPUs.
sacctmgr manages accounts and associations. But Slurm only applies the limits when enforcement is on.
So let's turn it on. The slurm section appends a line to slurm.conf that enforces associations and limits.
Accounts form a tree: physics may use four CPUs in total, and theory, one level down, lets each user run a single job at a time.
The Linux group physics just shares the name with the account. The two are unrelated.
Every node gets these users, with matching identifiers, and a shared home. alice works in theory, bob in both accounts, coordinating physics, and carol is an operator.
And dave? No account at all. Keep an eye on him.
Last, the software. Set CVMFS to true under storage, and every node mounts it read-only, even workers you add later.
Repositories mount on demand, as on bare metal. They come from the Docker host, or from a CVMFS volume plugin.
Without either one, leave the storage section out.
The file is ready. Run sind create cluster with the config flag, and the prompt returns once everything is in place.
To work as a user, put the name in front of the node for sind ssh, or use the user flag of sind exec and sind enter.
Under the hood, sind waited until slurmctld had registered the cluster, then built this tree with sacctmgr.
physics carries the CPU limit, theory the job limit, and bob shows up twice, once in each account.
With enforcement on, the cluster tests your policy. alice can run one job at a time.
All of physics shares four of the six CPUs, so a job that would need a fifth CPU stays pending in squeue.
And dave gets nowhere: Slurm rejects his sbatch. No account, no association, no job!
So, one file models your site. Accounts need a db node, limits need enforcement, and CVMFS comes from the host or a plugin.
Next up: rehearse a change, before production sees it. See you there!
